# Data Preprocessing and Normalization


## Overview
Data Preprocessing and Normalization prepares volumetric data for compression and rendering by ensuring format compatibility, correcting metadata errors, and mapping value ranges to standardized intervals [G]. This family operates on data layout and physical units to ensure integrity before compression or rendering occurs [G].

## Shared principles
This family shares no specific algorithmic mechanism beyond the general goal of preparing data for the [Compression](4-compression.md) pipeline [G]. Each child method addresses a distinct aspect of data integrity or range mapping [G].

## Subtopics

### [Volume Normalization](1823-volume-normalization.md)
Volume Normalization scales a volume tensor to the range $[0, 1]$ while ensuring constant positive masks are preserved as full foreground ($1.0$). It differs from general value compression by focusing on range mapping rather than bit-depth reduction, and from sparse structures by operating on dense data layouts [G].

### [Volume Utility Functions](2677-volume-utility-functions.md)
Volume Utility Functions are a collection of low-level helper routines used to prepare, validate, and transform volumetric data for compression and rendering pipelines [G]. They solve problems related to tensor dimensionality alignment, physical unit normalization (Hounsfield units), spatial resampling, and memory layout corrections. Unlike [Sparse structures](5-sparse-structures.md) which organize data topology, or [Value compression](6-value-compression.md) which reduces bit-depth, these utilities ensure data integrity and format compatibility before compression or rendering occurs [G]. They serve as the foundational preprocessing and postprocessing steps for the [Compression](4-compression.md) pipeline [G].

### [Dataset Preprocessing (DeepLesion)](7228-dataset-preprocessing-deeplesion.md)
Preprocessing steps for the DeepLesion dataset to prepare tomographic images for training, involving Hounsfield Unit conversion, thresholding, and cropping [G].

### Density Range Restriction and Ramp Function
#### definition
- [S1, unofficial] A preprocessing function applied to volume data to restrict the range of density values, improving compression ratio by removing irrelevant data and avoiding discontinuities that generate high frequencies.
#### step
- [S1, unofficial] Apply function $T$ to each density value: if density $\le d_1$, set density $= 0$; if density $\ge d_3$, set density $= 0$; if $d_1 \le$ density $\le d_2$, set density $= (\text{density} - d_1) \times d_2 / (d_2 - d_1)$; if $d_3 \le$ density $\le d_4$, set density $= (d_3 - \text{density}) \times d_4 / (d_4 - d_3)$.
- [S1, unofficial] Normalize models with histograms outside the $[0, 255]$ range to achieve the same output value range after applying $T$.
#### parameter
- [S1, unofficial] $d_1, d_2, d_3, d_4$: Threshold parameters defining the density range $[d_2, d_3]$ to keep intact and the ramps $[d_1, d_2]$ and $[d_3, d_4]$ to avoid discontinuities.

## Background
The concept of restricting density ranges to improve compression ratios was introduced in the context of volumetric medical images visualization on mobile devices [S1, unofficial]. The specific utility functions for Hounsfield unit normalization and tensor manipulation are derived from modern deep learning and graphics pipelines [G].
